title: Signal attenuation lab notes: noisy-slow-drifts-and-pager-calibration
content:
Summary:

This is a working scratchpad for experiments and runbook steps aimed at diagnosing and mitigating a class of observability problems we've been seeing: gradual metric attenuation (signals slowly decaying or disappearing), high-frequency low-value pager traffic triggered by derivative-based SLO rules, and intermittent missing-metric windows from exporters or scrape failures. Goal: capture hypotheses, quick mitigations, PromQL/splunk queries, experiment proposals, and comms templates so on-call can act consistently.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- Multiple pages in last 6 months with similar patterns but different root causes.
- Existing playbooks are either too heavy (full incident postmortem) or too specific (single exporter). Need a mid-weight lab notebook to iterate on fixes.
- Want repeatable debouncing experiments and a library of guardrails (synthetic heartbeats, sampling windows, alert grouping).

Observed example patterns (recent):
- Pattern A (slow fade): 03:00–08:00 UTC daily window where downstream latency metrics go flat for a subset of pods; dashboards show steady request rate but histogram buckets collapse to zero over ~15–30 minutes. No obvious CPU/memory spike.
- Pattern B (derivative squeal): Spike in SLO burn alerts from derivative-of-success-rate rule after a deployment with identical error rate but slightly different response structure (client-side code mis-parsed 204->200 and SRE rule flagged as anomaly).
- Pattern C (scrape dropout): Node exporter missing metrics for 60–90s followed by burst of high cardinality alerts as aggregators interpret missing as zero.

Hypotheses (do not assume):
1) Aggregation-level downsampling + short hiccups => zeros interpreted as sustained drop by rollup logic.
2) Exporter churn (OOMKill, threadpool starvation) causes inconsistent metric emission, only visible in high-cardinality subsets.
3) Alert rules using rate() or increase() with aggressive windows amplify transient blips into sustained alerts.
4) Beacon/heartbeat metrics missing from some stacks; lack of explicit sentinel causes missing->zero semantics.

Queries and quick-diagnostics (copy in on-call chat):
- Check cardinality + per-instance:
  - PromQL: topk(20, count by (instance) (up == 0)) or count by (job,instance) (absent(up))
- Identify zeros vs scrape gaps (use timestamp differences):
  - PromQL: (time() - max(timestamp(my_metric)) by (instance)) > 60
- Derivative alert debugging: compare raw rate vs long-window rate
  - prom: rate(success_count[1m]) and rate(success_count[15m])
- Example synthetic heartbeat check: last_over_time(heartbeat_metric[5m]) < 1 => potential missing exporter

Immediate mitigation playbook (for on-call):
1) Triage (0–10m):
   - Open the SRE incident channel and paste minimal context (service, alert name, top-3 affected instances).
   - Run the cardinality check and timestamp gap queries above.
   - Determine if event is cluster-wide, zone-limited, or single-node.
2) Short-term hush (10–25m):
   - If pattern is missing-scrapes causing floods, temporarily mute noisy alert rule(s) scoped to the noisy dimension using alertmanager silence targeted at the affected job/instance tags.
   - If SLO burn is derivative-squeal after deploy, mute derivative rule and open a rollback investigation; enable manual acceptance window for 15m.
   - DO NOT mute global SLO rules unless coordinated with product/CS. Document silence scope and expiration.
3) Root-cause checks (20–60m):
   - Check node/pod OOMs/kills: kubectl get pods -o wide; describe on affected pods; check kubelet logs.
   - Check exporter logs (filebeat, node-exporter): last 100 lines for stack traces.
   - Check recent daemonset restarts and config pushes (gitops PRs).
4) Communication (ongoing):
   - Post concise status updates every 20–30 minutes to incident channel. Include: actions done, next steps, ETA for unmute.

Recommended Prometheus/alert tuning checklist (medium-term):
- Replace immediate zero-sensitivity rules with absence() or timestamp-gap checks for exporters (explicitly prefer absent/last_over_time semantics to avoid zero confusion).
- For derivative-based SLO rules, require sustained degradation over >= 5 samples OR a quantile-based guard: e.g., require 3/5 buckets exceed threshold before SLO burn triggers.
- Add cardinality caps and blacklist for ephemeral labels that cause noisy splits (container_id, ephemeral_ip). Use labeldrop relabeling in scrape configs.
- Instrument synthetic heartbeats at the same cardinality as the real metrics (one heartbeat per service shard) so silence vs missing is explicit.
- Implement alert grouping by root-cause tag (node, job, region) and set group_wait to 30s and group_interval to 10m for noisy rules.

Experiment proposals (lab):
- Experiment 1: Debounce wrapper for SLO burn alerts
- Implement an alert template that requires three consecutive evaluations of burn > threshold across sliding windows (1m eval interval, require 3 evals).
- Measure reduction in page count and mean time to detection.
- Metrics: pages/day, pages/incident, detection-latency. Owner: Marco.
- Experiment 2: Last-timestamp-based exporter health
- Add a metric exporter_last_seen{job,instance} with timestamp; create alert if time() - max(timestamp(exporter_last_seen)) > 90s.
- Rationale: differentiates between zeros and missing scrapes. Owner: Evelyn.
- Experiment 3: Synthetic heartbeat shim for legacy exporters
- Deploy lightweight sidecar to emit a low-cardinality heartbeat metric for services that cannot be changed. Use fluentd/metrics-shim. Owner: Daniel.

Longer-term engineering priorities:
- Revisit all SLO/alert rules older than 18 months; add metadata on intended cardinality and expected failure modes.
- Central alert catalog: add tags like "zero-sensitive" and "derivative-guarded" and require review before enabling.
- Build a small internal dashboard: "metric health map" showing last_seen per exporter/job/region and rolling-cardinality.
- Run weekly chaos experiments for telemetry: intentionally drop scrapes for 30s to validate alert behavior and grouping.

Runbook snippets to standardize in Confluence (copy/paste-ready):
- Silence template: /alertmanager silence --match job="<job>" instance="<instance>" reason="temp-silence for exporter scrape gap" expires="15m"
- Pager triage checklist: 1) scope 2) mute minimal 3) root-cause checks 4) escalate if >30min unresolved.

Communication template for customers (if external-facing SLA risk):
- "We observed intermittent metric collection issues impacting telemetry for <service>. This affected our monitoring visibility but application traffic remained nominal. We have applied temporary mitigations to suppress noise and are investigating the telemetry source. We'll update by <ETA>."

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many alert rules in prod treat missing as zero vs using absent()? (Metric: count(alerts where expr contains '== 0' or 'sum() == 0').)
- Do we have a standardized heartbeat library across languages? (I think not.)
- Is there a quick way to surface relabel configs that cause label explosion? (Maybe a scraper audit job.)

Action items (short):
- Aisha: prototype exporter_last_seen metric in telemetry-config repo (PR done by 2026-03-20).
- Marco: run debounce experiment on non-prod SLOs by 2026-04-02.
- Evelyn: deploy heartbeat shim to canary namespace and monitor for 1 week; report on noise reduction. Due 2026-03-31.
- Daniel: compile list of top-30 noisy alert rules and their cardinality, share in SRE weekly. Due 2026-03-17.

Notes to self (chaotic):
- Keep this doc intentionally messy; it's where we iterate. If something becomes stable, move to canonical Confluence runbook with clear playbook steps.
- Remember to update linked_artifacts to include the chaos experiment results and any GitHub PRs.

Recent related tickets (context):
- SRE-7123: "Intermittent exporter gaps -> pager flood" (investigation ongoing).
- SRE-6998: "Derivative SLO false-positive post-deploy" (rollback pattern documented).

End of lab notes.

(If you landed here on-call: copy queries, run triage checklist, and ping @eng-sre in #sre-incidents channel)
